results.checks: A bybit_coverage_soak row exists in which the SIDE-AWARE grade actually DISAGREED with the side-blind sum (verdicts_differ: true). That is the load-bearing half of this row's threshold: a soak of any length in which the two never diverge shows the gate would change nothing on this book, so a bare row COUNT is not the criterion and the probe deliberately does not test one. The positive control (verdicts_differ present as either true or false) is what separates 'the gate ran and always agreed' from 'the log is absent or unreadable' -- and here that distinction is load-bearing rather than decorative, because 'nothing matched' is the state this row is ALREADY expected to be in, so an unreadable log would emit exactly the answer a reader anticipates. Measured 2026-09-02 the whole file held 28 rows, all with verdicts_differ false, so the control passes today while the requirement does not.
results.is_not: A PASS DOES NOT CLEAR THIS ROW, and specifically does not satisfy either clause of clears_when. It cannot see the ROW COUNT or the DAY SPAN (>=20 rows over >=3 distinct UTC days), because probe_soak tests for the existence of a matching row and not for a distribution -- so a single disagreement on one day passes this probe and clears nothing. It also cannot make clause (b), which is an OPERATOR DECISION to arm or not to arm; no probe can stand in for that. [!] A FAIL IS NOT EVIDENCE THE GATE IS INERT EITHER: the honest reading of a fail is 'no disagreement has been observed YET', and distinguishing that from 'this gate would never disagree' needs the day span the probe cannot measure. [!] AND IT SAYS NOTHING ABOUT WHETHER THE GATE IS ARMED -- it reads the annotate-mode soak, which is written whether or not BYBIT_GRADED_COVERAGE_ACCOUNTS names an account. Arming is confirmed on /proc/<MainPID>/environ via get-env, never from this log and never from the .env file.
